creature.name: ratewise
creature.tagline: Human-readable transfer rates, ETAs and data budgets: '3 GB at 25 MB/s' → '2m'.
creature.concept: A tiny library and CLI for anyone who moves data: parse sizes ('1.5 GB') and rates ('100 Mbit/s', '20 GB/day'), format rates back for humans, estimate how long a transfer takes, and compute how much data fits in a time window. Useful for download managers, backup scripts, CI logs and capacity planning.
creature.newCapability: Rates: sizes divided by durations. Neither donor can parse '20 GB/day', convert it to bytes per second, or answer 'how long will 3 GB take at 25 MB/s?'.

api.name: parseSize
api.description: Parses '1.5 GB', '2 KiB', '100 Mbit' or a bare number of bytes into bytes. Bits are divided by 8. Returns NaN for unrecognised text.

api.name: parseRate
api.description: Parses '<size>/<duration unit>' such as '5 MB/s', '20 GB/day', '100 Mbit/s' into bytes per second. Returns NaN for unrecognised text.

api.name: formatSize
api.signature: formatSize(bytes: number, options?: { binary?: boolean, bits?: boolean }): string
api.description: Formats bytes with 3 significant digits, e.g. 1337 → '1.34 kB'.

api.name: formatRate
api.signature: formatRate(bytesPerSecond: number, options?: { per?: 's'|'m'|'h'|'d', binary?: boolean, bits?: boolean }): string
api.description: Formats a rate, e.g. 1337 → '1.34 kB/s'; with bits, 12500000 → '100 Mbit/s'.

api.name: eta
api.signature: eta(size: number|string, rate: number|string, options?: { long?: boolean }): string
api.description: How long a transfer takes, as a short ('2m') or long ('2 minutes') duration.

api.name: budget
api.description: Bytes transferred at a rate over a duration (milliseconds or text like '1h').

tests.test: parseSize treats a bare number as bytes
parseSize returns NaN for unrecognised text
parseRate understands duration units like ms does
parseRate returns NaN without a time unit or for nonsense
formatSize uses 3 significant digits and decimal units
formatSize supports binary and bit units
formatRate can express the rate per day
eta gives a short duration for text inputs
eta gives a long duration on request
eta accepts raw numbers (bytes and bytes per second)
budget multiplies a rate by a duration
budget output reads naturally through formatSize
